hypotheses.paper: Troyanov's condition as cited at l.1930: 0 < sum(theta_i - 2pi) + 4pi <= min(4pi, theta_i : i)
hypotheses.here: replaced by the condition of record (DEC-174)
hypotheses.note: GX.TroyanovAngleConditionC is Theorem C's condition on the sphere (MR1005085 p. 795, papers/gx/sources/MR1005085/NOTE.md): 0 < chi' < 4pi and chi' < 2 theta_j for every j, chi' = sum(theta_i - 2pi) + 4pi = 2pi chi(S^2) + sum(theta_i - 2pi). The printed condition is exactly this plus chi' <= theta_j for every j (GX.troyanovAngleCondition_iff_troyanovAngleConditionC), so GX.TroyanovTheoremC is stronger than the printed form (GX.TroyanovTheoremC.troyanovTheorem): Lean >= paper.

hypotheses.paper: Theorem C: theta_1 <= ... <= theta_n positive numbers; the bound min{4pi, 2 theta_1}
hypotheses.note: No order on the angles is assumed: the condition is symmetric, and with a monotone theta it is verbatim 0 < chi' < min(4pi, 2 theta_0) (GX.troyanovAngleConditionC_iff_of_monotone); with theta_min the least angle (Finset.inf') it is verbatim 0 < chi' < min(4pi, 2 theta_min) (GX.troyanovAngleConditionC_iff_inf'). Positivity is derived (TroyanovAngleConditionC.pos).
Not assumed: Theorem C's condition forces s >= 3 on the sphere (TroyanovAngleConditionC.three_le; at s = 2 it reads theta_1 + theta_2 < 2 min(theta_1, theta_2)).

hypotheses.here: proved for s <= 4 and for all angles <= 2pi; the rest a tagged sorry
hypotheses.note: From the strict library, under Theorem C's condition: all angles < 2pi by GX.exists_isConeSphere_of_subcritical (whose hypotheses are Theorem C's); angles 2pi removed and re-added (GX.IsConeSphere.insertNth); s = 3 (every angle < 2pi there); s = 4 with an angle above 2pi by GX.exists_isConeSphere_dart, every hypothesis of which follows from Theorem C's condition (h23 from chi' < 2 theta_1 and theta_0 > 2pi). Left: s >= 5, no angle 2pi, some angle above 2pi (GX.troyanovTheoremC, DEC-136, T-gx-troyanov). No named hypothesis.

sorries.obstruction: Troyanov's existence theorem, T-gx-troyanov: a spherical cone sphere with s >= 5 prescribed angles under Theorem C's condition, none equal to 2pi, some above 2pi (possibly >= 4pi). MR1005085's proof is variational; the library's doubles of embedded polygons (GX.StarPolygon.isConeSphere) give only angles < 4pi, and no construction for this case is written. The sorry sits under GX.troyanovTheoremC_of_five_le_of_exists_gt_two_pi, so it carries only that case.

findings: l.1930 cites Troyanov (MR1005085) for a narrower condition than his Theorem C (p. 795). Exactly: the printed 0 < chi' <= min(4pi, theta_i : i) is Theorem C's 0 < chi' < min{4pi, 2 theta_min} together with chi' <= theta_j for every j (GX.troyanovAngleCondition_iff_troyanovAngleConditionC, 0 sorry). So the printed condition implies Theorem C's (GX.TroyanovAngleCondition.troyanovAngleConditionC) and the paper's use of the citation stands; the converse fails. Counterexamples with cone spheres built in the library: (7pi/5, 13pi/10, pi) at s = 3, chi' = 17pi/10 > pi = theta_2 (GX.troyanovAngleConditionC_three_not_printed); (5pi/2, 9pi/10, pi, 11pi/10) at s = 4, one angle above 2pi, chi' = 3pi/2 > 9pi/10 = theta_1 (GX.troyanovAngleConditionC_four_not_printed). Both tuples are pairwise distinct, so they also meet the cex's genericity (l.1935). Not a defect: the paper claims only sufficiency ('as long as'). The difference is theta_min where Troyanov has 2 theta_min; the paper's '<=' where Troyanov has '<' is harmless, since chi' <= theta_j < 2 theta_j and chi' = 4pi is never attained.

Theorem C's condition is sufficient, not necessary, for a spherical cone sphere, as the paper's is: the football with two angles pi is a cone sphere and fails it at s = 2 (GX.exists_isConeSphere_not_troyanovAngleConditionC).
questions: DEC-174 names GX.TroyanovTheorem only. The statement of the cex row itself (GX.TroyanovSuspensionTheoremS3, GX.ThurstonSuspensionFacts and DEC-69's GX.TroyanovSuspensionTheorem in scaffold TroyanovAngles and GX/SingularII/Models.lean) still quantifies over the printed condition. Reading taken: they keep the printed condition, which is l.1930's, and stay derivable from the new Prop. A probe confirmed that GX.troyanovSuspensionTheoremS3_of GX.troyanovTheoremC.troyanovTheorem GX.thurstonSuspensionFacts typechecks as GX.TroyanovSuspensionTheoremS3. Should the suspension statements also move to Theorem C's condition? That would be stronger than the paper, and it would need ThurstonSuspensionFacts for the wider set of angle tuples.

Not a reading, checked in Lean: whether theta_min in Theorem C ranges over all angles or only over those != 2pi makes no difference (GX.troyanovAngleConditionC_iff_ne_two_pi). A bound chi' < 2 * 2pi at an angle 2pi is the bound chi' < 4pi. Accordingly, adding or removing a marked point of angle 2pi preserves the condition (GX.troyanovAngleConditionC_removeNth_iff). Strict '<' in both bounds, as Theorem C and DEC-174 print it.

kb_proposals: Troyanov's condition of record is GX.TroyanovAngleConditionC (DEC-174), Theorem C's 0 < chi' < 4pi with chi' < 2 theta_j for every j (scaffold Spherical/TroyanovTheoremC). DEC-69's GX.TroyanovAngleCondition is the paper's narrower citation: it equals C plus chi' <= theta_j for every j (troyanovAngleCondition_iff_troyanovAngleConditionC). C alone forces s >= 3 and positive angles, and it is invariant under adding or removing angles 2pi (troyanovAngleConditionC_removeNth_iff), so the two-pi reduction ports verbatim.

The strict Troyanov constructions already work under Theorem C's condition. The hypotheses of GX.exists_isConeSphere_of_subcritical are Theorem C's. At s = 4, every hypothesis of GX.exists_isConeSphere_dart follows from C once the angle above 2pi is put at index 0; h23 comes from chi' < 2 theta_1 together with theta_0 > 2pi. So the C-form of Troyanov is proved for s <= 4 and for all angles <= 2pi (troyanovTheoremC_four, troyanovTheoremC_of_le_two_pi), and the open case is again s >= 5 with an angle above 2pi, now over a wider set of tuples (troyanovAngleConditionC_five_not_printed).
